title.narrative: Oc In 1.6. of funded agribusinesses that implement green economy activities

description.narrative: Green economy activities will help both SHFs and enterprises become more resilient to the negative impacts of climate change. This indicator measures how many funded agribusinesses implement green economy activities to aid building resilience to climate shocks, and therefore the impact EZCF has on preparing participants for the impacts of climate change. In order to fulfil this indicator, enterprises will be assessed on various criteria. They will need to demonstrate that they have done one or more of the following:1. Provided training to SHFs on climate smart practices,2. Implemented CS practices within their operations,3. Reduced their energy budgets.Additional information regarding green economy activities will be captured through the impact assessment, which will also capture the extent to which SHFs are implementing CS practices (such as soil mulching, drip irrigation, use of solar and biogas energy, etc)

title.narrative: Oc In 1.7. of funded agribusinesses that implement nutritionrelated activities

description.narrative: Measures the impact funding agribusinesses has on nutrition. Given that the programme works through enterprises rather than working directly with rural communities, it is important to adopt a multifaceted approach when assessing enterprises efforts to improve the nutritional status of smallholder farming households.Count the number of agribusinesses that implement nutritionrelated activities based on what activities are reported in the quarterly reporting template and quarterly report activities matrix. Agribusinesses can be categorised as either yes, nutritionrelated activities are implemented or no, nutritionrelated activities are not implemented. To fulfil the indicator, an enterprise will have to meet any of the following criteria: (a) producing/retailing nutritionenhanced products that support healthy diets and improve food and nutrition security, (b) developed and implemented strategy/plan to strengthen nutrition information through training/capacity building of smallholder producers linked to enterprise, or (c) developed and implemented workplace nutrition programme to improve the nutritional status of the enterprises workforce.

title.narrative: % of HHs with increased/improved assets

description.narrative: Description of the indicator: This indicator determines what assets households have access to (both productive assets such as iron, stove and luxury assets such as sofa, television) and whether assets are increased or improved across the duration of the project. Baseline value: 0Target value:80% of households by project endWhat does it measure: This indicator measures households levels of access to assets typically purchased with disposable income, indicating whether they were able to acquire greater assets over the course of the project. Changes in asset ownership over time is often used as a proxy to assess changes in poverty levels beyond changes in household income. It is easier for rural populations to recall changes in asset ownership than to recall accurate income data. How to measure it: Measure by asking head/representative of household whether the household owns the following items:Does this household own a television? Does this household own a gas or electric stove? Does this household own a lounge suite or sofa? Does this household own an iron? Is your house connected to electricity? Compare whether household assets increase/improve from baseline to endline assessments. Data source/means of verification: Impact AssessmentFrequency of data collection:Baseline and Endline
